topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: Add interop devstack preset with follow source (light CL) and exercise LocalSafe divergence
topIssues.author: opsuperchain
topIssues.body:
We need a devstack preset that combines follow source (light CL) with interop and supernode, and a test that exercises the follow source code path in that topology.

Today the follow_l2 tests (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/follow_l2/`) run against a single-chain `SysGo` preset (`WithSingleChainTwoVerifiersFollowL2`). In a single-chain setup without interop, `LocalSafeL2` and `SafeL2` (cross-safe) are always equal — the cross-safe promotion happens immediately after local-safe. This means the existing tests can't distinguish whether a follower node is correctly using `LocalSafeL2` vs `SafeL2` from its upstream source.

With interop + supervisor/supernode, cross-safe promotion is delayed by cross-L2 dependency verification, so `LocalSafeL2` and `SafeL2` actually diverge. This is the only topology where a test can verify that the follow source correctly plumbs `LocalSafeL2` separately from `SafeL2`.

### What's needed

1. **New preset** (e.g. `WithTwoL2SupernodeFollowL2`) that sets up:
   - Two L2 chains with interop enabled
   - Supernode as the shared consensus layer
   - At least one verifier per chain configured with follow source (light CL mode)
   - A derivation-enabled node as the follow source target

2. **Test** that exercises the follow source path and asserts:
   - The follower node's `LocalSafeL2` advances independently of `SafeL2`
   - `LocalSafeL2` leads `SafeL2` during the window before cross-safe promotion
   - Both eventually converge

This would provide integration coverage for the fix in `lightnode/localSafe` (which added `LocalSafeL2` to `FollowStatus` and `FollowSource()`), where the unit test alone can verify correct field copying but can't exercise the actual divergence in a running system.

Related: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19272

topPRs.title: fix(contracts-bedrock): remove artifact pulling, use unoptimized builds for CI tests
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Removes the GCS-based artifact caching system from contracts CI and replaces it with simple unoptimized builds for PR test jobs. The caching system caused stale artifacts, profile mismatches, and non-deterministic artifact resolution (#19323).

**PR test jobs**: New `liteci` profile (`optimizer=false`, 128 fuzz runs). Compiles from scratch — no GCS pulls, no caching. Fast enough without optimizer.

**PR build/check jobs**: Still use `ci` profile (`optimizer=true`) for size-check, snapshots, interfaces, semver, kontrol, docker.

**Develop post-merge**: Test jobs use `ci` profile to mirror production bytecode.

### Fork test fix for unoptimized profiles

CREATE2 produces different implementation addresses with unoptimized bytecode. Most proxies are re-pointed during OPCM upgrade so their validator checks pass, but DelayedWETH and ETHLockbox proxies are NOT re-pointed — they retain mainnet's optimized implementations. Fixed by conditionally mocking `getProxyImplementation` for these proxies when running with an unoptimized profile.

### Unified `skipIfUnoptimized`

Renamed `skipIfCoverage` to `skipIfUnoptimized` and expanded it to also skip when the Foundry profile is unoptimized. Both coverage instrumentation and unoptimized builds change bytecode in ways that break gas measurement tests and bytecode verification tests.

### Removed

- `pull-artifacts.sh`, `publish-artifacts.sh`, `use-latest-fallback.sh`, `calculate-checksum.sh`
- `publish-contract-artifacts` job and `develop-publish-contract-artifacts` workflow
- `install-zstd` command, `pull-artifacts-conditional` command
- `publish_contract_artifacts_dispatch` pipeline parameter

### Profile summary

| Profile | Optimizer | Fuzz runs | Used where |
|---------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| `ci` | true, 999999 | 128 | Build job (all branches), test jobs (develop only) |
| `liteci` | false | 128 | Test jobs (PRs only) |
| `ciheavy` | false | 20000 | Heavy fuzz (PRs), nightly heavy fuzz |
| `cicoverage` | false | 1 | Coverage jobs |
| `lite` | false | 8 | Local dev (`just test-dev`) |

### Bonus fix

Fixed a TOML ordering bug in the `lite` profile where `additional_compiler_profiles` and `compilation_restrictions` were nested under `[profile.lite.invariant]` instead of `[profile.lite]`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (contracts tests compile from scratch with `liteci` profile)
- [ ] Build job still produces optimized artifacts for checks
- [ ] Develop post-merge runs tests with `ci` profile

topPRs.title: fix(contracts-bedrock): make CI reliable
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fixes `VerifyOPCM_Failed()` CI failures caused by `vm.getCode("ProxyAdmin")` non-deterministically resolving to the `dispute` compiler profile's artifact (optimized with 5000 runs) instead of the default profile's artifact (999999 runs).

### Root cause

When `additional_compiler_profiles` is configured in `foundry.toml`, `vm.getCode(name)` can resolve to any matching artifact. For contracts compiled under both `default` and `dispute` profiles (e.g., `ProxyAdmin`), the resolved artifact is non-deterministic, causing bytecode mismatches in `VerifyOPCM` assertions.

### Fix

1. **`DeployUtils.getCode()`** — New wrapper that constructs the explicit artifact path (`forge-artifacts/<Name>.sol/<Name>.json`) to always resolve the default profile. Wrapped in `try/catch` so the Go script host in `op-chain-ops` (which doesn't support artifact paths but has no profile ambiguity) gracefully falls back to `vm.getCode(_name)`. Callers passing qualified identifiers (`:` or `/`) are passed through as-is.

2. **Migration** — 12 `vm.getCode()` call sites across 4 files migrated to `DeployUtils.getCode()`.

3. **Semgrep rule** — Bans direct `vm.getCode(...)` usage outside `DeployUtils.sol` to prevent regressions.

4. **L1ChugSplashProxy gas test** — Under `cicoverage`, the fix changes which artifact is loaded (from accidentally-optimized dispute artifact to correctly-unoptimized default). The larger bytecode shifts gas dynamics in the OOG test. Uses generic `vm.expectRevert()` for unoptimized profiles (the test still verifies the revert occurs, just without matching the specific error string).

### No Go changes

The `try/catch` fallback eliminates the need for any `op-chain-ops` modifications.

## Files changed (vs develop)

| File | What changes |
|------|-------------|
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/libraries/DeployUtils.sol` | Add `getCode()` with try/catch fallback; use in `create1`, `create2`, `createDeterministic` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/ChainAssertions.sol` | 5x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/DeployImplementations.s.sol` | 5x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol` | 1x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/L2/FeeSplitter.t.sol` | 1x `vm.getCode` → `DeployUtils.getCode` |
| `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/legacy/L1ChugSplashProxy.t.sol` | Add `cicoverage` condition + generic `vm.expectRevert()` for unoptimized |
| `.semgrep/rules/sol-rules.yaml` | Ban `vm.getCode(...)` outside DeployUtils.sol |
| `.semgrep/tests/sol-rules.t.sol` | Test cases for the semgrep rule |

topPRs.title: op-node: copy LocalSafeL2 in follow source mode
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# Tool Use Notice
Generated and Self Reviewed. May compact the testing.

# What

When op-node runs in light-node/follow-source mode, it follows an upstream node's sync status. Previously, FollowClient.GetFollowStatus() only copied SafeL2, FinalizedL2, and CurrentL1 - but not LocalSafeL2.

The FollowSource() function was incorrectly using SafeL2 (cross-safe) for updating the local-safe head, when it should use the upstream's LocalSafeL2 instead.

Changes:
- Add LocalSafeL2 field to FollowStatus struct
- Copy LocalSafeL2 from upstream sync status in GetFollowStatus()
- Update FollowSource() to accept separate LocalSafe parameter
- Pass LocalSafeL2 through followUpstream() to FollowSource()

# Tests
- Add test for FollowClient to verify LocalSafeL2 is copied. This also verifies _all_ fields are correctly copied.
